place.zh: 石坳村 · 屋后柴垛 · 半夜

setup.zh: 它一整天没醒，尾根的断口渗着银色的血。半夜里，它睁开了一只眼睛。你问她：真的有仙人？
setup.en: It has not woken all day; silver blood seeps from the cuts at its tail. At midnight it opens one eye. You ask her: are there really immortals?

recap.zh: 半夜里银月醒了一会儿：仙人是真的，凡人能修，一万个里不到一个——「剩下的，去问他们。」
recap.en: At midnight Yinyue woke a while: immortals are real, mortals can cultivate, fewer than one in ten thousand — "The rest, ask them."

zh: 柴垛上，一团凉冰冰的银毛。
断口渗出的血，是银的，像落了一层霜。
半夜，它睁开了一只眼睛。
en: On the woodpile, a cold curl of silver fur.
The blood from its cuts is silver, like a fall of frost.
At midnight, it opens one eye.

story.zh:
那天夜里，你把"围脖"抱回了屋后的柴垛上。

它一整天都没醒。身子是凉的，那一条尾巴垂着，尾根上那八道断口，不知什么时候又渗出了血——不是红的，是银的，一滴一滴，落在柴草上，像落了一层霜。

你守到半夜。

半夜里，它睁开了一只眼睛。

⟪「……吵死了，」⟫它的声音很小，⟪「你喘气那么大声干什么。」⟫

你松了一口气，一口气松得太猛，差点哭出来。你憋住了。

「银月，」你小声说，「你今天说，你是从仙界掉下来的。」

⟪「嗯。」⟫

「仙界……在哪儿？」

⟪「上面。」⟫

「比蒙山顶还高？」

⟪「……高多了。」⟫

你想了想。有一个问题，你从谷底憋到现在，憋了一整天。

「那……真的有仙人？」

银月睁开了另一只眼睛，看着你。

「吴婆婆讲过，」你说，「蒙山顶上住过一个白胡子老头，骑白鹤，一顿饭吃一颗枣，活了八百岁。我爹说，那是编的。」

⟪「你爹说错了。」⟫

你的嘴慢慢张大了。

⟪「仙人是真的。」⟫银月说，⟪「活八百岁的，有；活八千岁的，也有。他们以前，也都是凡人——猎户，樵夫，种地的，读书的。后来学会了一样本事，把天地间的灵气收进身子里，炼成自己的，一年一年，不老，不病，力能搬山，最后连天都关不住。」⟫

⟪「这就叫修仙。」⟫

柴垛上很静。你听见自己的心在咚咚地跳。

「那……我也能？」

⟪「能。」⟫银月说，⟪「但很难。一万个凡人里，能修的，不到一个。能修的人里，一百个，九十九个老死了事。」⟫

「那剩下那一个呢？」

银月没有马上回答。它看着你，看了很久，然后，它的眼睛慢慢合上了一半。

⟪「……你还有很多要问的，」⟫它的声音越来越低，⟪「本王知道。可本王……答不动了。」⟫

「那我问谁？」

⟪「问他们。」⟫它说，⟪「这世上，有一群人，专门修仙，专门教人修仙。他们会告诉你，灵气是什么，丹田是什么，境界是什么……比本王，有耐心。」⟫

它顿了顿，嘴角似乎翘了一下。

⟪「……当然，没本王教得好。」⟫
story.en:
That night you carry the "scarf" out to the woodpile behind the house.

It has not woken all day. Its body is cold, its one tail hangs limp, and at the tail's root the eight cuts have begun to bleed again — not red but silver, drop by drop, onto the straw, like a fall of frost.

You keep watch until midnight.

At midnight, it opens one eye.

⟪"…So noisy,"⟫ it says, very faintly. ⟪"Why are you breathing so loud?"⟫

You let out your breath, so hard you nearly cry. You hold it in.

"Yinyue," you whisper, "you said today you fell from the immortal realm."

⟪"Mm."⟫

"Where… is the immortal realm?"

⟪"Up."⟫

"Higher than the top of Mount Meng?"

⟪"…Much higher."⟫

You think. There's one question you've been holding in since the valley floor — a whole day.

"Then… are there really immortals?"

Yinyue opens its other eye, and looks at you.

"Granny Wu tells a story," you say. "An old man with a white beard lived on the top of Mount Meng; he rode a white crane, ate one jujube a meal, and lived eight hundred years. My father says it's made up."

⟪"Your father is wrong."⟫

Slowly your mouth falls open.

⟪"The immortals are real,"⟫ says Yinyue. ⟪"Some live eight hundred years; some live eight thousand. They were all mortals once — hunters, woodcutters, farmers, scholars. Then they learned one thing: to draw the spirit qi of heaven and earth into their bodies and refine it into their own, year after year — not ageing, not sickening, strong enough to move mountains, until at last not even heaven can hold them."⟫

⟪"That is what cultivating immortality means."⟫

It is very quiet on the woodpile. You can hear your own heart thumping.

"Then… could I?"

⟪"You could,"⟫ says Yinyue. ⟪"But it's hard. Of ten thousand mortals, fewer than one can cultivate at all. And of those who can, ninety-nine in a hundred grow old and die with nothing to show."⟫

"And the one left over?"

Yinyue doesn't answer at once. It looks at you, a long time, and then its eyes slowly half close.

⟪"…You've got plenty more to ask,"⟫ it says, its voice sinking lower and lower. ⟪"This king knows. But this king… can't answer any more."⟫

"Then who do I ask?"

⟪"Ask them,"⟫ it says. ⟪"In this world there are people who do nothing but cultivate, and teach others to. They'll tell you what spirit qi is, what a dantian is, what the realms are… more patiently than this king."⟫

It pauses, and the corner of its mouth seems to lift.

⟪"…Not as well as this king, of course."⟫
